Title: Tacos al Pastor with Marinated Pork and Pineapple
Servings: 4

Ingredients (component | amount unit | name | prep_style | pantry food_id):
- Al Pastor Pork | 500 g | pork shoulder |  | 000032
- Al Pastor Pork | 2 tsp | Chili Powder |  | 000653
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | smoked paprika |  | 000291
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | Garlic Powder |  | 000643
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | Ground Onion |  | 000644
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | ground cumin |  | 000278
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | dried oregano |  | 000257
- Al Pastor Pork | 1 tsp | salted butter |  | 000211
- Al Pastor Pork | 100 ml | pineapple juice |  | 000599
- Al Pastor Pork | 30 ml | White Vinegar |  | 000637
- Corn Tortillas | 8 pcs | tortilla |  | 000339
- Garnish and Salsa | 150 g | pineapple |  | 000158
- Garnish and Salsa | 50 g | onion |  | 000111
- Garnish and Salsa | 20 g | cilantro |  | 000245
- Garnish and Salsa | 2 pcs | lime |  | 000131

Steps in order (component | phase | minutes | text):
1. Corn Tortillas | Prep |  | Remove the corn tortillas from their packaging and separate them.
2. Garnish and Salsa | Prep |  | Remove the skin and core from the pineapple and cut into small 1cm cubes.
3. Al Pastor Pork | Prep |  | Thinly slice the pork shoulder into 1cm wide strips. SAFETY: Wash hands and all surfaces thoroughly after handling raw pork.
4. Corn Tortillas | Cook |  | Preheat a dry flat griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
5. Garnish and Salsa | Prep |  | Finely dice the white onion into a uniform brunoise.
6. Al Pastor Pork | Prep |  | In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the pineapple juice, white vinegar, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, and salt.
7. Corn Tortillas | Cook |  | Place a tortilla on the hot surface for approximately 30 seconds until it begins to puff slightly.
8. Garnish and Salsa | Prep |  | Wash the cilantro thoroughly, pat dry, and roughly chop both the leaves and tender stems.
9. Al Pastor Pork | Prep |  | Submerge the pork strips into the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1-2 hours to allow the enzymes to tenderize the meat.
10. Corn Tortillas | Cook |  | Flip the tortilla and heat the other side for 20-30 seconds until warm and pliable.
11. Garnish and Salsa | Prep |  | Cut the limes into eighths to create serving wedges.
12. Al Pastor Pork | Cook |  | Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat with a teaspoon of oil until shimmering.
13. Corn Tortillas | Serve |  | Stack the warmed tortillas inside a clean kitchen towel or tortilla warmer to maintain heat and moisture.
14. Garnish and Salsa | Cook |  | Optional: Quickly toss the pineapple chunks in the pan used for the pork for 2 minutes to caramelize the sugars.
15. Al Pastor Pork | Cook |  | Sear the pork in small batches to avoid crowding the pan, cooking for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply charred on the edges.
16. Garnish and Salsa | Serve |  | Combine the diced onion and chopped cilantro in a small bowl to create a fresh taco relish.
17. Al Pastor Pork | Cook |  | Verify the pork has reached an internal temperature of 63°C before removing from heat.
18. Al Pastor Pork | Serve |  | Let the meat rest for 5 minutes, then roughly chop into small bite-sized pieces for taco filling.
19. Garnish and Salsa | Serve |  | Set out the pineapple, lime wedges, and onion-cilantro mix in separate serving dishes for custom assembly.
